# Rask

> Rask is a C# component framework (Blazor-like) for .NET 10: a Roslyn factory generator,
> scoped CSS/JS, routing, and a live diff runtime over WebSockets (Server) or JSImport/JSExport
> (WASM). Components are plain C# classes; markup is written with generated factory methods and a
> children indexer (`Div()[Span(), "hi"]`).

This file helps AI coding assistants build apps with Rask. Start with AGENTS.md (in any
`dotnet new rask-*` project) for app-authoring conventions, then the docs below.

## Docs
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, first app, project layout.
- [Best practices](docs/best-practices.md): production patterns + common pitfalls across components, state, forms, data, security, accessibility, performance, testing (each links the deep dive).
- [Elements & the DSL](docs/elements.md): the render surface — the primitives (`Text` HTML-encodes, `Raw` is verbatim, `Doctype`) and the `[...]` collection expression for sibling fragments; a generator-emitted factory for every HTML and SVG element; the universal props (`Id`/`Class`/`Style`/`Data`/`Role`/`TabIndex`/`Aria`, fixed attribute render order) on every tag; typed SVG components (no `Raw()`); and the full HTML-element catalog by category.
- [Routing](docs/routing.md): `[Route]`, params, `Router()`/`Outlet()`, navigation.
- [Lifecycle](docs/lifecycle.md): OnMount/OnPropsChanged/OnRendered/OnUnmount, async hooks.
- [Composition](docs/composition.md): children, context (provide/consume), callbacks, flash messages (Rails-style `IFlash` — scoped-per-session, consumed-once transient messages that survive a client-side navigation; drained by a headless `FlashOutlet`, or `Rask.Bootstrap`'s ready-made `BsFlash`), the full DOM `GlobalEventHandlers` event surface on every element (mouse/pointer/touch/wheel/focus/keyboard/clipboard/drag as typed `OnX`+`OnXAsync` pairs; Audio/Video add the `HTMLMediaElement` events), headless primitives (`VirtualizeModel<T>`), drag-and-drop.
- [Forms](docs/forms.md): binding, validation, EditContext, building form components — implement `IFormControl<T>` (Rask.Core.Forms) on a generic component and the generator synthesizes its controlled + bound factories, or use the public binding API directly (`ExpressionAccessor`/`BindingHelpers`/`RegisterFieldValidator`). `IFormControl<T>` is the framework primitive; ready-made `BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup`/`BsMultiSelect` typed controls now ship in the optional Rask.Bootstrap package (the samples keep copyable build-your-own versions).
- [Bootstrap (Rask.Bootstrap)](docs/bootstrap.md): optional package of typed Bootstrap 5.3 component factories (`BsButton`/`BsCard`/`BsModal`/…), zero-JS interactive components driven by the live runtime (`BsModal`/`BsOffcanvas` incl. responsive drawer/`BsAccordion`/`BsTabs`/`BsDropdown`/`BsToast`, controlled state), SPA-routed navigation (`BsNavbar`/`BsNav`/`BsNavItem`, auto-active via `NavLink`), `IFormControl<T>`-bound inputs (`BsInput`/`BsSelect`/`BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup`/`BsMultiSelect`), color modes (`BsTheme`), a typed `BsIcon`, and typed utility classes (`Bs.Join(Shadow.Sm, Margin.Bottom(4, Bp.Md))`); bundles Bootstrap 5.3.8 + Bootstrap Icons 1.13.1 as static assets, linked with `BootstrapStyles()`.
- [Building form controls](docs/building-form-controls.md): end-to-end guide to authoring a custom control with `IFormControl<T>` — the interface, a complete worked example, the default-method helpers, and the bound-vs-controlled / stateless-helper-vs-Component trade-offs.
- [HTTP & files](docs/http-and-files.md): data & file *transfer* — a DI'd `HttpClient` (constructor-injected, `BaseAddress` at the app origin; fetch in `OnMountAsync` with cancel/retry/error handling), the typed file-picker input (`Input(Type: InputType.File, OnFiles:)` + `RaskFile` metadata; multipart on Server, JS chunked reads on WASM), and `Navigator.Download` (event-handler-only; served from `/_rask/download/…` on Server, base64 to JS on WASM).
- [Data access](docs/data-access.md): EF Core + SQLite, IDbContextFactory, loading in the lifecycle, vertical slices, DDD value objects, SQLite decimal gotcha.
- [CQRS](docs/cqrs.md): the opt-in, standalone `Rask.Cqrs` package — a source-generated, reflection-free CQRS/mediator. IQuery<T>/ICommand/ICommand<T>/INotification + their handlers, dispatched via a single IDispatcher — DispatchAsync (one method for queries and commands, response type inferred) and PublishAsync for notifications; register with AddRaskCqrs(). Handlers are wired by a Roslyn generator (no runtime reflection, no assembly scanning, [DynamicDependency]-preserved ctors) so it publishes clean under the WASM/AOT trimmer. Pipeline behaviors (IPipelineBehavior<TRequest,TResult>, registered via AddOpenBehavior / AddBehavior) are the decorator hook for logging/validation/etc; none ship. Notifications fan out Sequential or WhenAll. Diagnostics RASK028 (ambiguous handler) / RASK029 (unregisterable handler). Depends only on Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions.
- [Browser APIs](docs/browser-apis.md): the map of all typed Web-API wrappers (43) — shared vs WASM-only, one-shot vs subscription, with the inject-from-ctor pattern and the push/[JSInvokable] mechanism.
- [JS interop](docs/js-interop.md): scoped CSS/JS, element refs, IJSRuntime, typed browser APIs — shared (both transports) in Rask.Core.Browser ( plus the PWA APIs IWebPush/INotifications/IBadge/IWakeLock); WASM-only in Rask.Wasm.Browser (IShare/IScreenOrientation/IFullscreen/IInstallPrompt + device APIs ISerial/IUsb/IHid/IBluetooth/IMediaDevices/IEyeDropper/IPictureInPicture/IIdleDetector).
- [Mobile & PWA](docs/pwa.md): build installable mobile apps in C#. WASM = full PWA (install, true offline, push, every device API). Server = installable + push-capable via AddRaskPwa (serves manifest + service worker, auto-registers it, emits the manifest link into the server-rendered head), but NOT an offline app (offline navigations show a static offline.html; no background sync; install-prompt + activation-bound device APIs stay WASM-only). Typed Web app manifest (WebAppManifest in Rask.Core.Browser; WASM UsePwa / Server AddRaskPwa), default service worker (rask-sw.js; shared push/notificationclick handlers in Rask.Core), IWebPush + INotifications + IBadge + IWakeLock (Rask.Core.Browser, both hosts), `dotnet new rask-wasm --pwa` / `dotnet new rask-server --pwa`. Sending push from the backend: the opt-in `Rask.WebPush` package (IWebPushSender, VAPID RFC 8292 + aes128gcm RFC 8291, zero external deps).
- [Authentication](docs/authentication.md): cookie/JWT, Authorize, route guards.
- [Observability](docs/observability.md): structured logging, the `Rask.Server` meter + activity source, `AddRaskLiveSessions()` health check.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): `RaskLiveOptions` (shared: diff mode, path base, session cap) + `RaskServerOptions` (server-only WS/grace/idle/backpressure limits) + `RaskUploadOptions` (upload size + per-session quota), appsettings binding + startup validation.
- [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md): ARIA via the `Aria` dictionary, `Role`/`TabIndex`, the `Img` alt-text analyzer (RASK023).
- [Migration from Blazor](docs/migration-from-blazor.md): mapping Blazor concepts to Rask.
- [Diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md): RASK001–024 compile-time diagnostics + fixes.
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): unit + Playwright E2E patterns.

## Contributing to Rask itself
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): repo conventions for AI assistants + the `.claude/skills/` workflows.
- [Development workflow](docs/development-workflow.md): the format → warnings-as-errors → tests →
  benchmarks → docs → review → PR gate, CI, nightly, analyzers.
- [Code analysis](docs/code-analysis.md): analyzers and adoption.
